facts.statement: The genus Tupuxuara was described by paleontologists Kellner and Campos in 1988.
facts.quote: authority: Kellner & Campos, 1988

facts.statement: Tupuxuara lived during the Albian age of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 million years ago.
facts.quote: Tupuxuara is a genus of thalassodromid pterosaur that lived during the Albian age of the Early Cretaceous, about 112 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossils of Tupuxuara were found in the Romualdo Formation of the Santana Group in Brazil.
facts.quote: Its remains were found in what is now the Romualdo Formation of the Santana Group in Brazil.

facts.statement: Tupuxuara possessed a large crest extending from the back of its head to its snout.
facts.quote: It had a big crest at the back portion of its head, stemming from the snout.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the crest size likely indicates sexual maturity, as it appears more prominent in mature individuals.
facts.quote: This crest is most likely an indicator of sexual maturity, given that it appears more prominently in mature individuals.

facts.statement: Tupuxuara had a toothless beak.
facts.quote: The beak of Tupuxuara was toothless.

facts.statement: Tupuxuara had an estimated wingspan of 4.7 meters and a body mass of 25 kilograms.
facts.quote: A wingspan of 4.7 m and a body mass of 25 kg have been estimated for Tupuxuara

facts.statement: Some studies argue Tupuxuara belongs in the family Thalassodromidae rather than Tapejaridae, based on a closer relationship with Azhdarchidae and Dsungaripteridae.
facts.quote: However, several studies have argued against this arrangement and have supported a closer relationship with the families Azhdarchidae and Dsungaripteridae, with Thalassodrominae being elevated to family level, thus creating the term Thalassodromidae.

facts.statement: Based on its lineage, Tupuxuara was likely a terrestrial omnivore or carnivore, contrary to earlier suggestions of a fish or fruit diet.
facts.quote: However, based on its azhdarchoid lineage, Tupuxuara most likely would have been a terrestrial omnivore or carnivore.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Tupuxuara longicristatus (MN 6591-V) was found in the Santana Formation, now called the Romualdo Formation, in Brazil.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MN 6591-V, was found in the Santana Formation (now known as the Romualdo Formation) of Brazil

facts.statement: A second species, Tupuxuara leonardii, was named in 1994 by Kellner and Campos.
facts.quote: In 1994, Kellner and Campos named a second species, Tupuxuara leonardii.

facts.statement: A third species, Tupuxuara deliradamus, was named in 2009 by Mark Witton.
facts.quote: In 2009, British paleontologist Mark Witton named a purported third species, Tupuxuara deliradamus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Tupuxuara deliradamus is a valid species, as it has been classified as a nomen dubium by Kellner in 2013 and by Cerqueira et al. in 2023.
facts.quote: However, this species has been considered as a nomen dubium (dubious name) by Kellner in 2013. A 2023 study by Brazilian paleontologist Gabriela Cerqueira and colleagues also classified T. deliradamus as a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Recent studies suggest Tupuxuara deliradamus should be removed from the genus Tupuxuara and placed in the subfamily Tapejarinae.
facts.quote: It was recovered as an indeterminate member of the subfamily Tapejarinae and as the sister taxon of the species Caupedactylus ybaka, effectively removing it from the genus Tupuxuara.

facts.statement: The most distinguishing feature of Tupuxuara is a large bone crest protruding from the back of its head to its snout.
facts.quote: The most distinguishing characteristic of Tupuxuara is the large crest that it possessed, which protruded from the back portion its head and originated from its snout.

facts.statement: The crest of Tupuxuara was more prominent in mature individuals.
facts.quote: This feature was more prominent in mature individuals.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Tupuxuara had a wingspan of 4.7 meters, a body length of 2 meters, and a mass of 25 kilograms.
facts.quote: In his 2022 pterosaur book, American paleontologist Gregory S. Paul indicated that Tupuxuara had a wingspan measuring 4.7 m, a total body length of 2 m and a body mass of 25 kg.

facts.statement: Tupuxuara was slightly smaller than its closest relative, Thalassodromeus.
facts.quote: Tupuxuara was slightly smaller compared to its closest relative, Thalassodromeus

facts.statement: Tupuxuara longicristatus was discovered in the Santana Formation in 1988 by Alexander Kellner and Diógenes Campos.
facts.quote: La especie T. longicristatus fue descubierta en la Formación Santana en 1988 por Alexander Kellner y Diógenes Campos.

facts.statement: The genus name Tupuxuara refers to a household spirit from Tupí mythology.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se refiere a un espíritu familiar de la mitología de los Tupí.

facts.statement: A second species, Tupuxuara leonardii, was named by Kellner in 1994.
facts.quote: En 1994 una segunda especie fue nombrada por Kellner: Tupuxuara leonardii.

facts.statement: Tupuxuara measured approximately 2.5 meters in length and 5.4 meters in wingspan.
facts.quote: Tupuxara medía unos 2,5 metros de largo y 5,4 m de envergadura.

facts.statement: Its main distinguishing feature was a large head crest that was more rounded in females and absent in individuals that had not reached sexual maturity.
facts.quote: Su principal rasgo distintivo era una gran cresta en su cabeza, más redondeada en las hembras y ausente en los individuos que no habían alcanzado la madurez sexual.

facts.statement: Its head, measuring nearly 1 meter, was enormous compared to the body and very lightweight due to holes in the skull.
facts.quote: La cabeza, que medía casi 1 m, era enorme a comparación con el cuerpo, era muy liviana gracias a los agujeros en el cráneo.

facts.statement: Mature individuals of T. longicristatus possessed a crest that curved backward and originated from the snout.
facts.quote: Los individuos maduros de T. longicristatus poseían una cresta vuelta hacia atrás que se originaba desde el hocico.

facts.statement: The largest skulls have a length of 130 centimeters, indicating a wingspan of 5.5 meters.
facts.quote: Los mayores cráneos tienen una longitud de 130 centímetros, indicando una envergadura de 5.5 metros.

facts.statement: Tupuxuara was a pterodactyloid pterosaur of the superfamily Azhdarchoidea that lived in the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian and Hauterivian stages) in what is now Brazil.
facts.quote: Tupuxuara (espíritu familiar) es un género de pterosaurios pterodactiloideos de la superfamilia Azhdarchoidea que vivió a principios del Cretácico (Valanginiense y Hauteriviense) en lo que hoy es Brasil.

facts.statement: Tupuxuara was initially assigned to the family Tapejaridae by Kellner, closely related to the pterosaur Tapejara.
facts.quote: Tupuxuara was initially assigned to the family Tapejaridae in its description by Kellner, closely related to the pterosaur Tapejara.

facts.statement: In 2007, Kellner and Campos placed Tupuxuara in the subfamily Thalassodrominae alongside Thalassodromeus.
facts.quote: In 2007, Kellner and Campos divided Tapejaridae into the subfamilies Tapejarinae and Thalassodrominae, with Tupuxuara being a member of the latter, alongside Thalassodromeus.

facts.statement: In 2006, David Martill and Darren Naish supported placing Tupuxuara and Thalassodromeus as sister taxa to the Azhdarchidae.
facts.quote: In 2006, this arrangement would be further supported by British paleontologists David Martill and Darren Naish, who found Tapejaridae to be paraphyletic (unnatural), and found both Tupuxuara and Thalassodromeus as sister taxa to the Azhdarchidae.

facts.statement: Kellner assigned Tupuxuara to the family Tapejaridae within Azhdarchoidea.
facts.quote: Kellner lo asignó a la familia Tapejaridae dentro de Azhdarchoidea.

facts.statement: According to some analyses, Tupuxuara is more closely related to the Azhdarchidae (the group that includes the giant Quetzalcoatlus of North America) than to Tapejara and its relatives.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, de acuerdo a algunos análisis, Tupuxuara es más cercano a los Azhdarchidae (el grupo que incluye al gigantesco Quetzalcoatlus de Norteamérica) que a Tapejara y sus parientes.

facts.statement: It has been suggested that Tupuxuara had a piscivorous diet preying on the coasts of modern-day South America, while some hypotheses include the possibility that it was a fruit eater.
facts.quote: It has once been suggested that Tupuxuara had a piscivorous (a fish-based) diet, preying in the coasts of modern day South America, while some deviant hypotheses even include the possibility that it was a fruit eater.

facts.quote: type_species: Tupuxuara longicristatus

facts.statement: The species included in the genus Tupuxuara are T. longicristatus, T. leonardi, and T. deliradamus.
facts.quote: subdivision: T. longicristatus Kellner & Campos, 1988 T. leonardi Nessov, 1991 T. deliradamus Witton, 2009

facts.statement: A subadult described by David Martill and Darren Naish in 2006 lacked a fully developed crest, supporting the suggestion that the crest was a marker for sexual maturity.
facts.quote: Un subadulto descrito por David Martill y Darren Naish de la Universidad de Portsmouth en 2006 aún no se había desarrollado plenamente su cresta, que apoya la sugerencia de que la cresta era un marcador para la madurez sexual.

facts.statement: Comparisons between the scleral rings of Tupuxuara and modern birds and reptiles suggest it may have been diurnal.
facts.quote: Las comparaciones entre los anillos escleróticos de Tupuxuara y las aves modernas y reptiles sugieren que puede haber sido diurna.
